extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to academic journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on what journals expect when declaring conflicts of interest (COI) in manuscript submissions, including what counts as a COI, what to disclose, and where/how to submit the declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor-provided definition of competing interest
rubrics_metrics.description: “A competing interest exists when professional judgment concerning the validity of research is influenced by a secondary interest, such as financial gain.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the journal's stated threshold for when a competing interest exists — any secondary interest (example given: financial gain) that could influence professional judgment should be considered a competing interest and disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: WAME definition of conflict of interest (COI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per WAME, a conflict of interest or COI "exists when a participant in the publication process (author, peer reviewer, or editor) has a competing interest that could unduly influence (or be reasonably seen to do so) his or her responsibilities in the publication process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this broader community standard to judge whether relationships or interests might 'unduly influence' responsibilities; the definition applies to authors, reviewers, and editors and includes both actual and perceived influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy of complete disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Most international journals follow a policy of complete disclosure when it comes to COI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, disclose. Journals generally expect authors to reveal all possible conflicts rather than selectively omitting items; transparency is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial and commercial relationships as potential COIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential conflicts could arise from financial relationships, including funding, grants, sponsorship, or commercial/financial relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement should acknowledge any kind of financial support received (funding, grants, sponsorship). Disclose commercial or financial relationships that might be viewed as a conflict in the cover letter or COI statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-financial sources of COI
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential conflicts may also arise from personal relationships or rivalries, academic competition, or differences in ideologies or beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COIs are not limited to money — interpersonal, competitive, or ideological factors that could influence judgment should be considered for disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation of absence of biasing agreements with sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should declare that they have not signed any agreement with the sponsor that will bias the results of their research in any way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, explicitly state that no contractual obligations to sponsors affect study design, data analysis, interpretation, or reporting; if restrictive agreements exist, disclose them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit negative declaration allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If you feel you do not have any potential conflict of interest, you should give a declaration mentioning that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an explicit statement such as 'The authors declare no competing interests' so the absence of conflicts is documented rather than omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the journal's specific COI form or requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the manuscript submission guidelines of the journal and see whether the journal has a specific form or any specific requirements for declaration of conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some journals provide their own COI disclosure forms or require particular wording/placement; conform precisely to those instructions when submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ICMJE guidance and form when journal lacks a form
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICMJE guidelines on conflicts of interest and their disclosure form can be used as a reference if the journal does not provide a form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the ICMJE guidance for a clearer view of what to disclose and use their standardized form as a template for completeness and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose COI in both manuscript and cover letter as appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Any commercial or financial relationship that might have the potential of being viewed as a conflict of interest has been disclosed in the cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Besides placing a COI statement in the manuscript, mention relevant conflicts in the submission cover letter if the journal requests or if relationships could affect editorial handling; be transparent at multiple submission touchpoints.
